rationale: bugs_open/049 mechanism 2: site chrome renders navigation links to pages that have NEVER been deployed, so the link 404s on EVERY page of the site. Measured live 2026-07-26 by fetching 229 active pages across 8 sites and probing all 274 unique internal targets over HTTPS: 118 broken anchor instances remain, and 40 of them come from just three nav items (gaswholesalers 'Pricing Framework' -> /fuel-pricing-framework.html, 28 instances = one per page; vetcomparison 'Find a Practice' and 'Guides', 12 more). A fleet census found 13 active nav items across 6 sites in this state. The intent of this change is to stop the renderer WRITING a link the platform's own audit then flags. The important part is that the obvious fix is wrong in BOTH directions and this change therefore converges on an already-measured predicate rather than inventing a third one. Today all three chrome call sites pass deployedOnly=false, which ships the dead links. Flipping them to deployedOnly=true is also wrong: that path filters on build_status = 'deployed', and measurement recorded in bugs_open/049 showed 34 of 34 pages that are needs_rebuild but were deployed once return HTTP 200, because a page deployed once keeps serving its old artefact — so deployedOnly=true would delete 34 working links to fix 13 broken ones. Its nav-tables form additionally reads 'AND (ni.page_id IS NULL OR p.build_status = 'deployed')', which deliberately KEEPS items whose page_id was set to NULL by ON DELETE SET NULL — that is 4 of the 13 census rows (leopardess). Only 'never deployed' predicts a 404, and that predicate already exists in this repo with its measurement attached, inside check_phantom_internal_links. This change moves it to datahelpers so the renderer that writes links and the audit that flags them decide by ONE definition instead of two that can drift, and replaces the deployedOnly bool with a named NavVisibility type so the compiler forces every call site to be re-read — a bool rename would not have, and the defect was precisely a 'false' that read as harmless. Risk is concentrated in one place: emptying a site's navigation. The invariant is that filtering can shrink a nav but never empty one — if the site has no deployed pages at all (a first build) or the lookup errors, the unfiltered nav is served and logged loud, matching the loud/quiet-empty precedent already in GetNavItems for bugs_open/053. That guard was wrong in the first draft and a new test caught it: it read 'if nothing survived, degrade', but loadFetchablePageSet always injects the site root, so 'Home' survived, the guard never fired, and a brand-new site would have frozen a one-item header into its chrome (RenderSiteComponentsAction skips re-rendering once rendered_html is non-empty, so that would persist indefinitely). It now keys on the site having no deployed pages, which is the thing actually being detected.

plan.summary: Chrome must not link a page that was never built. Move the measured never-deployed predicate to datahelpers so the nav renderer and the phantom-link audit share one definition; replace GetNavItems' deployedOnly bool with a NavVisibility named type; filter on URL (not page_id) after the query, with a first-build degrade that can never empty a nav.

edits.rationale: One definition of 'this page would 404', reachable by both the renderer that writes links and the audit that flags them. datahelpers is the neutral lower layer both already import; putting it in discovery_checks would make the render path depend on the audit package and invert the layering. It sits beside PageURLSet because it answers in SQL exactly what PageURLSet answers in Go.

+// the column names are UNQUALIFIED and so valid only in a FROM pages with no

edits.rationale: The core change. A named type instead of a bool so the compiler stops at every call site (a rename would not break compilation, so nobody would re-read them). Both query builders lose their deployment predicate and their SQL LIMIT; one Go-side filter now serves both source paths, so the nav-tables path and the pages fallback cannot drift. Filtering on URL rather than page_id is what catches items orphaned to page_id IS NULL, which the old predicate explicitly kept.

The reported defect's site. All four nav loads here become <a href> in chrome that ships on every page of the site, so an unbuilt target is a site-wide 404. The old 'runs during build when pages may not be deployed yet' justification is now handled inside GetNavItems, which degrades rather than emptying.

grounded_in: // deployedOnly=false: runs during build when pages may not be deployed yet.
const neverDeployedPredicate = `deployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(build_status, '') <> 'deployed'`
// It is `deployed_at IS NULL`, NOT `build_status <> 'deployed'`. Measured across
// the fleet on 2026-07-20 against live HTTP:
//	needs_rebuild AND deployed_at IS NOT NULL   34 pages — 34/34 return 200
//	deployed_at IS NULL                         22 pages — every one tested 404s
page_id UUID REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
// Only fall back when the site has no nav-table rows at all; otherwise respect
// the truthful empty answer. Gating on the per-group row count instead let a
// be a fresh instance of the platform's silent-empty-render class
